stories.title: Abu Dhabi trilateral talks end without breakthrough
stories.summary: Trilateral talks in Abu Dhabi involving Russia, Ukraine and the United States concluded after a second day without any concrete agreement to end the war that began with Russia’s 2022 invasion. The U.S. side said it saw “some openings,” but no breakthrough was announced. On Thursday, Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner are scheduled to travel to Moscow and Dublin for separate meetings with the Russian and Ukrainian presidents.
stories.why: The talks are a high‑level diplomatic channel that could shape future attempts to resolve the Russia‑Ukraine conflict.

Moscow and Kyiv said a large‑scale prisoner‑of‑war exchange is being prepared and could be carried out soon.

stories.title: Alberta issues wildfire advisories and warnings in November
stories.summary: A Global News report notes that unusually warm conditions in November have prompted Alberta to issue wildfire advisories and warnings. The province maintains an Alberta wildfire status page and uses its emergency alert system to inform residents about fire risk and ongoing fire activity.
stories.why: Timely alerts help residents take protective actions and enable authorities to allocate resources effectively.

stories.title: Anthropic IPO draws overwhelming demand, could raise up to $90.4 billion
stories.summary: Anthropic PBC’s initial public offering has attracted an overwhelming response, with investor demand potentially amounting to $90.4 billion. The company is projecting a market valuation of about $1.4 trillion and reported a revenue run‑rate of $81 billion as of 31 October. Goldman Sachs is acting as the lead manager for the offering.
stories.why: The strong demand signals high investor confidence in Anthropic and could bring significant capital into the AI sector.

stories.title: Global Market Today: Asian stocks mixed as Nvidia turmoil hits AI-linked shares
stories.summary: Nasdaq 100 futures fell over 1% and S&P 500 contracts lost 0.5% after Nvidia tumbled about 10% in late trading. The New York Times also reported Wednesday that Huang had a relationship with Nvidia healthcare vice president Kimberly Powell, citing multiple people who worked at the company.

stories.title: With $720M round, Britain’s Fractile gets a leg up in the race for AI chips
stories.summary: Fractile, a British startup developing AI chips, has raised a $720 million Series C backed by Britain’s Sovereign AI Fund with hopes of “ensuring the U.K. Alongside the likes of Axelera, Etched, and OLIX, this makes Fractile one of the top-funded startup players in the race for purpose-built AI chips.
stories.why: This matters because it could change AI capabilities, costs, adoption, regulation or competitive positioning.
stories.previousTitle: British AI chip startup Fractile raises $720 million Series C
stories.previousSummary: Fractile, a UK‑based AI‑chip developer, announced a $720 million Series C round led by Thrive Capital, Founders Fund, Lightspeed Venture Partners and Redpoint, with participation from Britain’s Sovereign AI Fund. The financing values the company at over £5 billion (roughly $7 billion) and supports its full‑stack approach that pairs a machine‑learning compiler with a DRAM‑stacked chip design aimed at lowering inference costs.

stories.title: Why the data center you dread might never even be built
stories.summary: Before those challenges even come into play, though, there’s a more basic problem: A lot of the projects being announced may never get built in the first place. On this episode of TechCrunch’s Equity podcast, hosts Rebecca Bellan and Tim De Chant are joined by Brent Nelson , senior managing director of markets and strategy at Ascend Analytics , to separate the data center projects that are likely to get built from the ones that may never get off the ground.
